html:
The Natya Shastra is a Sanskrit handbook on theatre, dance and music, credited to the sage Bharata. It was put together between about 200 BCE and 200 CE and is the base of all the classical performing arts of India.

It has about 6,000 verses in 36 chapters. It covers how to build a playhouse, the plots of plays, costume and make-up, the tuning of instruments, and above all the body: it lists 108 dance poses and names the hand gestures, eye movements and steps an actor must learn.

Its central idea is rasa, "taste". A play succeeds when the audience tastes a lasting mood: love, laughter, sorrow, anger, courage, fear, disgust or wonder. The actor's job is to build that mood, not to copy life. Later critics, above all Abhinavagupta in Kashmir, made rasa the centre of Indian thinking about art.

The plays of Kalidasa follow its rules. The dance forms now called classical, such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak and Odissi, all trace their grammar of gesture to it. The 108 poses are carved on the gateways of the temple at Chidambaram.
sum: The Natya Shastra is a Sanskrit handbook on theatre, dance and music, credited to the sage Bharata. It was put together between about 200 BCE and 200 CE and is the base of all the classical performing arts of India.
